concepts.simple_definition_amharic: [አማርኛ] INTRODUCTION 147 UNIT 7: MACROECONOMIC REFORMS IN ETHIOPIA UNIT 7 MACROECONOMIC REFORMS IN ETHIOPIA INTRODUCTION Economic reform began throughout Africa in the mid-1990s (ይህ ትርጓሜ በኢትዮጵያ የ12ኛ ክፍል ሥርዓተ-ትምህርት መሠረት የተዘጋጀ ነው)።

concepts.simple_definition: 7.1 National Development Objectives and Strategies- Historical Review 149 UNIT 7: MACROECONOMIC REFORMS IN ETHIOPIA 7.1.1 National Development Plan during the Imperial Period (1950-74) When their occupation of Ethiopia ended in 1941, the Italians left behind a country whose economic structure was much as it had been for centuries, although there had been some improvements in communications, particularly in the area of road building, and attempts had been made to establish a few small industries and to introduce commercial farming
concepts.deep_explanation: During the late 1940s and the 1950s, much of the economy remained unchanged
concepts.real_example: Practical example of 7.1 National Development Objectives and  from page 159.
concepts.common_confusion: Students sometimes confuse 7.1 National Development Objectives and  with adjacent topics in Chapter 7.

concepts.deep_explanation_amharic: [አማርኛ ማብራሪያ] During the late 1940s and the 1950s, much of the economy remained unchanged — ይህ ጽንሰ-ሐሳብ ተማሪዎች በክፍል ውስጥ የተማሩትን በቀላሉ እንዲረዱ ይረዳቸዋል።

concepts.simple_definition: 7.1 National Development Objectives and Strategies- Historical Review 150 Grade 12 Economics Student Textbook The Second Five-Year Plan (1962 –1967) Similarly, the second Five-Year Development Plan (1962-1967) continued to prioritize industrial development
concepts.deep_explanation: Large-scale commercial farms for production of cotton, coffee and sugar were promoted as a source of income over small-scale subsistence farms, which accounted for about 80% of cereal production

concepts.common_confusion_amharic: [አማርኛ] ተማሪዎች ይህንን ጽንሰ-ሐሳብ ከሌሎች ተዛማጅ ርዕሶች ጋር ሊያደናግሩ ይችላሉ።

concepts.simple_definition: 7.1 National Development Objectives and Strategies- Historical Review 151 UNIT 7: MACROECONOMIC REFORMS IN ETHIOPIA Ethiopia enjoyed an annual average growth rate of 4% in percapita gross domestic product
concepts.deep_explanation: The manufacturing sector’s growth rate more than doubled (from 1.9% in 1960/61 to 4.4% in 1973/74), and the growth rate for the wholesale, retail trade, transportation, and communication sectors increased from 9.3% to 15.6%
